solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 25 across to 26); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charlie left party knocking back cocktail

indicators.note: knocking back a drink tips it towards you, so the preceding letters are read from the end

blocks.note: Charlie and snow are both slang for cocaine
L is the abbreviation for left
Lab is short for the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A drug user leaves a party after downing a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the left-plus-party pair is turned round; the drug slang stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowball is a mixed drink of advocaat and lemonade, popular at Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: Deputy that might make you resign!

blocks.note: straight reading: the officer ranked just below the chief
setter's reading: read the phrase as an order to sign a second time, and re-sign is what you would do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Resign' looks like quitting; split it as re-sign, and the phrase becomes an instruction to put your name down again.
explanation.definitionFit: The person next in rank to a commander, standing in for them, is a deputy.

clue.text: Old player finally cut deck

indicators.note: finally points to the very end letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the final letter of player
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A veteran card player finally cuts the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' in the card setting is a pack; here it is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Show disapproval of couple grabbing black bird

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to boo is to show disapproval
B is the abbreviation for black
to couple is to link

explanation.surface: Jeer at a pair who catch a blackbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' reads as one thing; black goes inside the jeer and bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobolink is a North American songbird of the blackbird family.

clue.text: A shopping district erected over Peruvian transportation

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting something sets it upright, so its letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A shopping centre built over transport links in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are Andean pack animals used in Peru for carrying loads, so they are a means of transport.

clue.text: Sailor left a mark

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A seaman's departure has left its mark on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is a sailor from India or Southeast Asia, historically employed on European ships.

clue.text: Very much an Arabian boat

blocks.note: taken as written
a dhow is a lateen-rigged Arab sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone is very fond of an Arab sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: 'And how!' is an emphatic exclamation of agreement, meaning very much indeed.

clue.text: Carried on chopping leaves for cooking

indicators.note: chopping cuts things up, so these letters are cut and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cook kept on chopping herbs for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a herb whose leaves, also called cilantro, are used in cooking.

clue.text: Odd plumber initially ordered little sinks for wee chap

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
ordered means put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
the first letter of plumber
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A strange plumber ordered small basins for a little boy, with 'wee' hinting at a toilet joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the tiny imp of the Grimm fairy tale, a little man.

clue.text: Liking charm when put under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one word under another places it after, lower in the column

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
to charm is to enchant

explanation.surface: Fondness for charm that persists under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or inclination for something, a fondness.

clue.text: Observe beetle and car crashing

indicators.note: things that crash are smashed up, so the letters of the words before it are broken and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Watch a VW Beetle and another car collide.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Beetle' as a make of car, 'Observe' looks like simply watching the crash; it means marking an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a festival or anniversary is to mark it ceremonially, which is to celebrate it.

clue.text: Wheat uni put in snare?

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a snare is a kind of drum
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Is the student's wheat being caught in a trap?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snare' suggests a trap; the question mark flags that it is the drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is a hard wheat variety ground for pasta and semolina.

clue.text: North-eastern China is a mountainous area

blocks.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-eastern
china means mate in cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), and a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: A geography fact: China's north-east is mountainous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in rhyming slang it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is the Himalayan country containing Everest, a fair example of a mountainous area.

clue.text: Cool city leader leaves farm with fruit that's not new

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and it departs from the word that follows
not new means without N, the abbreviation for new

blocks.note: a ranch is a farm; its first letter goes
an orange is a fruit; its N goes

explanation.surface: A trendy city's mayor quits the farm, taking along some stale fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is Alaska's largest city, and its cold climate makes it literally cool.

clue.text: Asian is carrying one son for another

definitions.note: another Asian, read from the first word

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an Indian is an Asian
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An Asian person carries one child on behalf of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian' looks like the definition but supplies the outer word; 'another' means another Asian, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Indonesia is a second nationality of the same continent as an Indian, so another Asian.

clue.text: Scare off short toilet cleaner

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to deter is to scare off
the gents is a British name for a men's toilet; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone scares off a person who cleans toilets for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, a substance for washing.

clue.text: Nervous picadors scattered

indicators.note: someone nervous is jittery and agitated, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Jittery mounted bullfighters fled in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: Picadors are the horsemen in a bullfight who use lances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring here and there or now and then, irregularly scattered.

clue.text: Price at which one may be disagreeing

definitions.text: at which one may be disagreeing

blocks.note: first meaning: the betting price offered on an outcome

blocks.clueFragment: at which one may be disagreeing
blocks.note: second meaning: people 'at' this word are in dispute

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition only works with the 'at' it mentions: to be at this word is to be in conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers quote a price as a ratio, and the idiom 'at odds' means in disagreement.

clue.text: Watches Durham, say, being contained by some bowling

indicators.note: being contained by means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: in cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled
Durham is a bishop's see, the 'say' marking it as one example

explanation.surface: Someone watches Durham's cricket team bowling, with the batsmen kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham looks like the cricket county; it is the diocese. An over is a cricket unit of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, which is to watch over others' work.

clue.text: Mention sex in church

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise the subject of sex during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to refer to or quote it, which is to mention it.

clue.text: Removed nit for upsetting Italian scorer

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and disorders it, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A footballer had his head lice dealt with, which upset him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a goalscorer; it means someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer of the early Baroque, and a composer scores music.

clue.text: Throw gold over Latin American dictator

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means flipped, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: to cast is to throw
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone throws gold at a South American strongman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro ruled Cuba, a Latin American country, as a one-party leader for decades.

clue.text: Kind of cat made alarm go off

indicators.note: something that goes off explodes or goes wrong, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cat set off the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmalade cat is a ginger tabby, named for the orange colour of the preserve.

clue.text: Special walk-on part

blocks.note: first meaning: additional, over and above the usual
second meaning: a non-speaking film or stage role

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a special cameo; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means additional or special, and also names a background actor in a crowd scene.

clue.text: Gay? Not born straight

indicators.note: not born means without B, the abbreviation for born

blocks.note: gay in its old sense of cheerful, bright

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is gay, and is told no, straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets gay against straight as sexual orientations; both are being used in other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Right in the sense of a right line or angle means direct and not bent, i.e. straight.

clue.text: Fertiliser sample of Nicaraguan origin

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from something larger, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A specimen of manure from Nicaragua.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is seabird or bat droppings, used as a rich fertiliser.

clue.text: Lively beer's right on time

indicators.note: on here means next to, so each piece follows the one before

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
R is the abbreviation for right
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bright, lively beer that arrives on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means quick and wide awake, so close in sense to lively.

clue.text: Not knowing when badgers might appear

blocks.note: first meaning: unaware, uninformed
second meaning, literal: badgers are nocturnal, so they come out at night

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading of the idiom for being uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in the dark is an idiom for ignorance, and it is also literally night-time.

clue.text: Place making car needs parking for it? That's unnecessary

indicators.note: something needing a replacement swaps one piece for another, with the 'for' saying which goes

blocks.note: Detroit is Motor City, home of the American car industry
P is the abbreviation for parking
taken as written; this is the part that is replaced

explanation.surface: A car factory wants parking provided, but someone dismisses this as superfluous.
explanation.walkthrough: The IT in the city's name is swapped for the parking letter, as 'for it' says.
explanation.definitionFit: De trop is French for too much, used in English for something superfluous or unwanted.

clue.text: Cut some butter to go on this snail

indicators.note: going on something means being placed after it, so the first word's letters follow the next

blocks.note: a ram is one animal that butts, a butter
shorn means cut, as of fleece

explanation.surface: Cut a bit of butter to put on this snail, as if cooking escargots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: The ramshorn is a freshwater snail with a flat coiled shell resembling a ram's horn.
